summary: The first cause is incomplete tin-variety metadata used by the already-ported eat.c consume_tin(): C selects dried tin (index 7) and adds 55 nutrition, while JS TIN_VARIETIES[7].nutrition is undefined. lesshungry(undefined) turns hunger into NaN, which the JS hunger classifier maps to FAINTING and newuhs() refuses at step 50. The newuhs annotation is the downstream stop site, not the source defect. The same reached tin also has separate skipped cprefx and lycanthropy/equipment effects; the later cursed-water action is not reached before this stop.

source.branch: In consume_tin(), after the player accepts non-spinach contents from an ordinary untrapped tin, tin_variety() returns DRIED_TIN (r=7) for this recording; the C tintxts[7] entry supplies nut=55 and greasy=0 before lesshungry().
callers: cmd.c's 'e' command table entry dispatches to eat.c doeat().
eat.c doeat() selects a tin and calls start_tin().
For the recorded easy-open occupation, eat.c start_tin() installs opentin(); eat.c opentin() calls consume_tin() when the opening delay completes.
The alternate zero-delay branch in eat.c start_tin() calls consume_tin() directly.
The JavaScript production route is js/cmd.js runEatCommand() -> js/eat.js doeat() -> start_tin() -> opentin() -> consume_tin().
dependencies: eat.c tin_variety() returns the variety index consumed by consume_tin(); the step-47 trace is rn2(15)=7 @ eat.c:1503, selecting the eighth tintxts[] entry.

eat.c tintxts[] at eat.c:138-159 defines dried as {"dried", 55, 1, 0}; js/eat.js TIN_VARIETIES index 7 has name and healthFood only, so nutrition and greasy are undefined. A generalized divergence fix should carry the C nutrition and greasy fields for every table row, while retaining the existing healthFood/fodder mapping.

C consume_tin() passes nutamt=55 to the void lesshungry(); lesshungry() adds it to u.uhunger and calls newuhs(FALSE). In JS, undefined + u.uhunger yields NaN, hungerStatus(NaN) falls through to FAINTING, and newuhs() throws its unsupported-transition marker. The valid C value does not request a fainting transition.

consume_tin() calls void cprefx(mnum) and cpostfx(mnum), discarding both results. JS records note_unported("eat.c cprefx"); cpostfx() recognizes PM_HUMAN_WERERAT but records note_unported("were.c set_ulycn") and note_unported("artifact.c retouch_equipment") for the C lycanthropy/equipment calls. Preserve these independent source gaps for follow-up; they do not produce the NaN nutrition stop.

CANNIBAL_ALLOWED() in eat.c:51 includes Race_if(PM_ORC), so the current Orc does not receive the non-Orc cannibal penalty in maybe_cannibal(); cprefx remains an explicitly recorded void gap, not the reason newuhs() refuses.
nethack-c/patches/README.md documents deterministic seed/time, stable sort, RNG logging, and screen-capture instrumentation; these patches do not alter the eat.c tin or hunger behavior.

evidence: Source: nethack-c/upstream/src/eat.c:138-160 defines tintxts[]; the dried row (index 7) is {"dried", 55, 1, 0}. eat.c:1488-1511 returns the tin variety, and consume_tin() at eat.c:1528-1700 selects that row and passes its nut value to lesshungry() at lines 1626-1631.

Recorded C evidence: challenges/cases/v17/orc-wizard-tin-lycanthropy-cursed-water-corrected-letters.session.json step 47 has key o and rn2(15)=7 @ tin_variety(eat.c:1503); step 48 smells like wererats, step 49 asks whether to eat it, and step 50 key y records "You consume dried wererat." The first C RNG on that step is rn2(5)=3 @ distfleeck(monmove.c:538), after C has completed the consumption and returned to the turn loop.

Saved evaluation: challenges/evaluations/20261001190602-v17.json reports 50/78 screens matched and a stop at step 50 in newuhs(); the queue records 28 remaining screens. The prior accepted-preparation row missionPlanEvidence.fullSourceActionCrosswalk.retainedCases[10] independently records the same step-50 boundary and C recording SHA-256 70af4f5e…08cc0d5e.

JavaScript: js/eat.js:431-449 defines TIN_VARIETIES without nutrition or greasy fields; js/eat.js:1076-1183 consume_tin() reads both. js/eat.js:2048-2105 lesshungry() adds the supplied number, and js/eat.js:573-583 hungerStatus() maps NaN through its comparison fallthrough to FAINTING; js/eat.js:1821-1850 then throws the recorded UnsupportedHungerTransitionError marker.

The stop annotation names eat.c newuhs(), but source order and state flow show it only consumes the invalid NaN produced by missing table data. Fix the data contract from C for the complete tintxts[] table; do not make newuhs() accept invalid numeric state.

The same accepted PM_HUMAN_WERERAT tin reaches C cpostfx() at eat.c:1129-1325; JS cpostfx() at js/eat.js:2514-2748 has explicit note_unported gaps for set_ulycn and retouch_equipment. The C call cprefx() is also represented by note_unported at js/eat.js:1159-1162. These are distinct remaining source effects, not the cause of the step-50 NaN stop. The recipe’s later cursed-water input has not yet been reached.
The six recorder patches listed in nethack-c/patches/README.md provide deterministic runtime, RNG, and screen capture and do not patch gameplay behavior in eat.c.
